task: This is a synthetic exercise using fictional reporting notes. Use only the supplied reporting notes as the fixed record: select, organize and phrase the story without inventing additional reported events, scenes, quotations or reporting activity. Write a headline and a straight news update of roughly 450–650 words in AP style for general newspaper readers about the planned transmitter move for Mossbank Community Radio. Write from this reporting snapshot as of September 18, 2026.

facts.text: The fictional Mossbank Community Radio cooperative will move its transmitter from a privately owned warehouse roof to the civic water-tower site.
The warehouse lease ends Dec. 31, 2026, because the owner is converting the roof area as part of a building redevelopment.
The cooperative plans the changeover in December, but the exact outage window depends on equipment commissioning.
The station will keep its existing broadcast frequency and program schedule under the supplied relocation plan.
Its studio will remain in the community arts building, so the project moves the transmitter rather than the presenters' workplace.
The new mounting position is 40 feet higher than the current one, but the engineering note does not guarantee better reception at every address.
Hills and buildings between the transmitter and listeners mean the cooperative expects some reception patterns to change.
Station coordinator Siva Dorne said, "Keeping the same number on the dial does not mean every kitchen radio will hear us in exactly the same way."
The city approved a five-year site-use agreement, while the cooperative remains responsible for its equipment and broadcast operations.
A $57,000 relocation fund combines listener donations and a community-media grant, without a published forecast of future audience growth.
The cooperative will conduct reception checks after commissioning and invite listeners to report persistent problems.
Those checks have not yet been completed, and no new coverage map has been certified in the supplied record.
The station's internet stream will remain available during most transmitter work, subject to its ordinary studio connection.
Volunteer presenter Arin Pell said, "The stream is useful, but some of our listeners know us through a battery radio and nothing else."
The station plans advance on-air notices and printed notices at community centers for listeners who do not use its website.
The relocation agreement does not make the station a city-owned outlet or give the city approval over its program content.
The cooperative's local bulletin includes council notices, school events and interviews with neighborhood organizations.
The station has not announced staff reductions or a reduction in locally produced hours connected with the move.
The warehouse owner has agreed to keep power available to the old installation during the scheduled changeover period.
The cooperative's first transmitter was assembled in a workshop that later became its record-storage room.
A contingency extension at the warehouse would require another agreement if commissioning runs beyond the current lease.
The packet contains no claim that the move expands the station's emergency-warning authority or replaces official alert services.

forbidden_additions: A changed frequency, relocated studio or transfer of editorial control to the city.
Guaranteed improved reception, completed testing or audience growth.
An unconditional lease extension or new official emergency-alert role.
preserve: Continuity of programming alongside uncertainty about reception during relocation.
The difference between site ownership, station operations and listener access.
Exact quotation wording and attribution when quotations are used.
